# Phase 1 probes (1.0) — background sessions on the installed CLI

*Source of record — do not edit.* Live probes from the execute session, Claude Code **2.1.296**,
macOS, throwaway detached worktree `~/claude-worktrees/spec-driven/crew-probe-p1` (removed after),
`--model haiku --permission-mode bypassPermissions`. If a crew run misbehaves on a newer CLI,
re-run these first.

## Answers

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| A `--bg` session idle on a background shell: its `state` | `status: busy`, `state: working` for the whole wait, even after its turn ended on text ("WAITING"). It is never `done` while a background shell runs. |
| Is it re-invoked when the shell exits? | Yes. The `<task-notification>` arrived as a user turn, it replied, then `idle` / `done`. |
| SendMessage to a `--bg` session **by id** | Fails. Neither the short id (`97434bde`) nor the full session id resolves: `No agent named '<id>' is reachable`. `ListAgents` shows the session by its `-n` name plus its own `[ref]` (not the `claude agents` id). **Sending by the bare `-n` name works.** |
| …while `done` | Delivered; the session runs a turn and answers. |
| …while `working` | Queued; delivered at its next tool round / turn end, and answered then. Survived a `kill -9` (below). |
| State after `kill -9` | For a few seconds the row reads `pid: null, status: null, state: working` (stale). Within ~15 s the background service **restarts the session** (new pid, same id and sessionId), it drains its queued messages and goes on. A killed worker is not `gone`; `SendMessage` then notes "messaging a new session for the first time under a previously used name". |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BG_EXIT_HANDOFF=1` on `claude stop` | `stop` killed the background shell (`sleep 240` gone, marker never written). **Control without the variable: same.** `stop` ends background shells either way; the variable only matters for a session exiting on its own. Keep it in the launch line (harmless, and it keeps exits from handing shells to the service). |
| Does `claude rm` delete the transcript? | No. `~/.claude/projects/<encoded cwd>/<sessionId>.jsonl` stays. `rm` drops the roster row and `~/.claude/jobs/<id>/`, and left the worktree (it was not created by `claude`). |
| After `stop` | Row stays with `pid: null, status: null, state: stopped` until `rm`. |

## Side findings

- **`--bg` stdout:** the first launch after the service is down prints `Starting background service…`
  before `backgrounded · <id> · <name>`; later launches don't. The parser must find the line, not
  take line 1. Fixture: `T/tests/fixtures/claude-bg-stdout.txt`.
- **Foreground `sleep` is blocked by the harness** inside a `--bg` session too; the worker refused
  `python3 time.sleep` as a workaround. Briefs must not ask workers to sleep.
- A worker that ends its turn on prose ("SLEPT not sent: …") reads `idle` / `blocked`, no
  `waitingFor` (confirms wave 2c).
- `~/.claude/jobs/<id>/state.json` carries `detail` and `needs` summaries; undocumented, don't build on it.

## Consequences for technical.md

- Messages go **by the worker's launch name** (`-n '<spec> execute <phase>'`), which is unique per
  launch; the id identifies it in the roster, `claude stop|rm|attach`. A name reused by a relaunch
  reaches the new session ("latest wins"), so the overseer only messages names whose id it launched
  and still sees in the roster.
- A babysitter on `pr wait` reads `working`, so the "babysitter, any state while its claim is live"
  row is belt and braces; `done` really means finished.
- `gone` is rare: `kill -9` is revived. A row with `pid: null` and a non-`stopped` state is
  transient: the roster wait treats it as no change and waits for the next poll.
- `claude rm` is safe for close-out: the transcript stays for later reading.
